fullPassage: Have you ever wanted to say something but found yourself struggling to remember the correct word? This is called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon. There are several different things that can cause it. In some cases, it happens because you feel exhausted. In other cases, it is caused by having a weak memory of the missing information. No matter what the cause is, you shouldn't struggle to remember the desired information, as this can make it more difficult to recall in the future. A better way of resolving the situation is to simply look it up online. Once you've found the word, you can break the cycle by repeating the word over and over, either aloud or silently. This creates something called a procedural memory, which will lower the chances of the word being forgotten again.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: resolve → resolving: 전치사 of 뒤에서 동명사(-ing)로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'a better way of __________'에서 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로, resolve를 resolving(해결하는 것)으로 바꿔요. of + 동명사 = ~하는 것의.

→ 따라서 resolve를 resolving으로 써요.
det.tip: way of + 동명사(-ing) = ~하는 방법.

questions.passage: Once you've found the word, you repeat it over and over until you remember it well. This creates something __________ (call) a procedural memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: call → called: 명사 뒤에서 '~라고 불리는'을 나타내는 과거분사로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'something __________ a procedural memory'에서 '~라고 불리는'이라는 수동의 뜻이 되어야 하므로, call을 과거분사 called로 바꿔요. something (that is) called ~ 에서 that is가 생략된 형태예요.

→ 따라서 call을 called로 써요.
det.tip: something called ~ = ~라고 불리는 것 (명사 + 과거분사).

questions.passage: Have you ever wanted to say something but found yourself struggling to remember the correct word? This is called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon. There are several different things that can cause it. In some cases, it happens because you feel exhausted. In other cases, it is caused by having __________ of the missing information. No matter what the cause is, you shouldn't struggle to remember the desired information, as this can make it more difficult to recall in the future. A better way of resolving the situation is to simply look it up online. Once you've found the word, you can break the cycle by repeating the word over and over, either aloud or silently. This creates something called a procedural memory, which will lower the chances of the word being forgotten again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a strong mind=강한 정신 / a weak memory=약한 기억 / a clear voice=맑은 목소리 / a fresh start=새로운 시작
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 'of the missing information(사라진 정보에 대한)'이 단서예요.

② a weak memory: 사라진 정보에 대한 '약한 기억' 때문에 설단 현상이 생긴다 ←정답

① a strong mind: '강한 정신'은 원인이 될 수 없어요

③ a clear voice: '맑은 목소리'는 문맥과 관련 없어요

④ a fresh start: '새로운 시작'은 문맥과 맞지 않아요
det.tip: caused by having ______ of the missing information → 약한 기억(a weak memory).

questions.passage: Have you ever wanted to say something but found yourself struggling to remember the correct word? This is called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon. There are several different things that can cause it. In some cases, it happens because you feel exhausted. In other cases, it is caused by having a weak memory of the missing information. No matter what the cause is, you shouldn't struggle to remember the desired information, as this can make it more difficult to recall in the future. A better way of resolving the situation is to simply look it up online. Once you've found the word, you can break the cycle by repeating the word over and over, either aloud or silently. This creates something called __________, which will lower the chances of the word being forgotten again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a procedural memory=절차 기억 / a physical injury=신체 부상 / a personal opinion=개인적 의견 / a random guess=무작위 추측
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'This creates something called ______(이것은 ~라고 불리는 것을 만든다)'과 뒤 '잊을 가능성을 낮춘다'가 단서예요.

① a procedural memory: 반복이 만들어내는 것은 '절차 기억'이에요 ←정답

② a physical injury: '신체 부상'은 문맥과 관련 없어요

③ a personal opinion: '개인적 의견'은 문맥과 맞지 않아요

④ a random guess: '무작위 추측'은 문맥과 맞지 않아요
det.tip: repeating → creates ______ → 절차 기억(a procedural memory).
